tasks.short: Turn yearly pay, benchmark and benefits findings into a manual, works council note or intranet guide.

today.trigger: Once a year after the salary review, benchmark update or CAO change, or when the works council or HR Director asks for a written account.
steps: Collect the year's analyses from Excel, AFAS extracts and Power BI screenshots
Decide the audience: managers, works council, employees
Write the text in Word with tables and charts, in Dutch and sometimes English
Check figures against AFAS and the CAO texts, anonymise small groups
Get review from HR Director and Payroll, then publish on SharePoint or Teams
drudgery: Rebuilding tables and charts by hand from Excel
Rewriting the same findings for three audiences
Checking that every number in the text matches the source
today.time_sinks: Formatting tables and charts, and the back-and-forth on wording with reviewers; the analysis itself is already done.

lenses.faster: An LLM drafts the text and audience versions from the analysis workbook, and charts come straight from Power BI, so the specialist edits instead of writes.
lenses.autonomous: Little runs alone: a yearly template refreshes its figures from the AFAS extract, but nothing is published without the specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Publish a plain reward guide for every employee group, including flex workers, and a yearly pay transparency explainer ahead of the first report over 2027 pay due 7 June 2028.
lenses.joy: No more retyping tables or reformatting charts; what is left is choosing the story and the wording for the works council.
lenses.options: Three versions from one source: a two-page manager brief, a works council note with method and caveats, and a short employee FAQ.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns one reward publication template with fixed definitions and sources, and checks each year's run instead of writing from scratch.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: standard pay dashboards and their written commentary
HR Business Partner: manager briefing packs on the salary review
Internal communication of benefits and pension changes such as the new Pensioenfonds Vervoer scheme

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what the works council and managers will read into a sentence, what may be shared under AVG and the CAO, and which caveats keep a number from being misused.
tasks.pattern_why: Low-volume, high-sensitivity writing for a known audience: AI drafts and formats, the specialist decides content, tone and what is disclosed.

in_practice.trigger: Specialist starts the yearly reward publication after the salary review or benchmark update closes.
steps: Point the assistant at the analysis workbook, Power BI export and last year's document
Assistant drafts the text, tables and audience versions in the house template
A script checks every figure in the draft against the source workbook and flags groups under the anonymity threshold
Specialist edits, adds caveats and sends to HR Director and Payroll for review
Specialist publishes on SharePoint and shares the works council version
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist and HR Director approve the final text before anything goes to the works council, managers or the intranet.
systems: Microsoft 365 Copilot or a Claude/ChatGPT enterprise workspace
data_needed: Aggregated pay and benefits analyses (no individual records in the prompt)
Last year's publication and house style
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint document version history with the source workbook and the figure-check result attached

evidence.claim: LLMs draft report text and summaries from tables and notes inside Word and Excel.
Pay transparency rules will require a yearly gap report, first over 2027 pay by 7 June 2028, with works council involvement, which raises the volume of written pay explanations.
Drafting audience versions and checking figures against a source cuts writing time roughly in half for a report like this.

risks: A drafted sentence overstates or misreads a figure and the works council treats it as an HR position
Small groups become identifiable, breaching AVG
Individual pay data pasted into a non-approved AI tool
Text reads generic and loses trust with managers and the works council
research_questions: Which reward documents does Noordhaven actually publish each year, and how many hours go into each?
Does the works council accept AI-drafted text if the method and sources are stated?
Can the figure check run reliably against the Power BI or Excel source without manual mapping?
Is Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed and approved for aggregated HR data at Noordhaven?

role.altitude: From grading jobs and writing reports one at a time to owning the job architecture, the reward data definitions and the evidence behind every pay difference, with AI producing drafts and figures that the specialist checks.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: pay gap and reward dashboards from AFAS
Payroll Specialist: CAO costing and checks on pay scale changes
HR Business Partner: manager briefings and first answers to pay questions
HR Administrator: benefits and pension questions answered by a gated agent
FP&A Analyst: personnel cost scenarios for salary review and CAO rounds
role.ceiling_note: Work with the works council, CAO parties, complaints and final pay decisions stays human: WOR consent rights, GDPR Art. 22 and the AI Act high-risk rules for grade or pay recommendations from 2 December 2027 cap autonomy at 2–3 for anything touching an individual's pay. Writing and data preparation can be cut by about half; the 1 FTE will not shrink much, it shifts toward pay transparency work.
skills_to_grow: Job evaluation on the four pay transparency factors and explaining it to the works council
Writing and checking prompts and templates for reward documents
Basic data modelling in Power BI and SQL on the AFAS extract
AI Act and GDPR obligations for HR systems: oversight, logging, transparency
Pay gap analysis and finding explanations for differences
role.ambitious_version: Noordhaven is ready for the Wet loontransparantie before it starts: every job, including flex roles, sits in a works-council-approved job architecture, every pay difference has a recorded reason, pay requests are answered within days instead of two months, and managers and employees get clear reward and benefits guides that update themselves each year.
